kitDescription: Sugar (Treasure) is an Iron shotgun Burst-III attacker whose passive keeps an Attack Damage buff running while her cover is intact and, from battle start, makes her damage count as elementally advantaged against Fire Code enemies. Every time the team enters Full Burst she gains Critical Rate and ATK for 10 seconds, stretches the magazine of every shotgun ally by 83.8% for 15 seconds, and grants Water/Iron shotgun allies extra elemental-advantage damage. When she casts her own burst she gains Attack Speed, Hit Rate, and ATK for 15 seconds, plus a stronger elemental-advantage damage buff for Water/Iron shotgun allies. Her treasure kit's cover-attacked crit-damage and reload-speed procs and the cover-HP restore are defensive/cover-state effects with no sim representation and are recorded as unmodeled.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs found. All 13 kit lines are FAITHFUL (10) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (3, the cover-attacked proc pair plus the cover-HP restore — verbatim in unmodeled with ⚑ recipes, exactly the S2b-sanctioned honest handling; no fabricated cadence anywhere). The two highest-risk decisions — S2 lines on fullBurstEnter vs burst lines on burstCast, and the SG-scoped max-ammo including self — were independently re-derived by S2b, S5, and S6 with identical trigger/stat/scope, and the driver's own spec pins each against a named counterfactual that goes RED (trigger flips, scope widening, removals), with the S2d matrix showing a non-zero damage delta for every encoded line. Convergence of the blind tests against the shipped override is GREEN (4/4 plus the blind's own self-skip; the only fixes were harness-API glue, assertions preserved). Two blind-side errors are logged as recon notes, not driver defects: both S2b and S6 read the SG max-ammo duration as 10s where the treasure prose (explicitly the SSOT per the characters.json note) says 15s — the driver's 15s is correct; and S2b's expectation that helm co-receives the SG buff rests on a roster misread (helm is SR), which the driver's dynamically-derived holder set handles robustly. Same-model residual the owner should spot-check: every agent shares the premise that the cover-intact Attack Damage line collapses to always-on under the immortal-boss model (⚑1) and that the count:99 alliesOfElementWeapon union encoding is the right schema idiom — both are documented conventions, but a fresh-eyes read of those two choices is the cheap residual check. Nothing must change for GO.
